←Module 1: Getting Started with Google Workspace
Lesson · 20 min

What Google Workspace Is

Meet the Google Workspace apps, learn how a personal Google account differs from a work account, and see how each Google app lines up with the Microsoft 365 app you may already know.

By the end of this lesson you can

  • ✓Name the main Google Workspace apps and what each one is used for at work
  • ✓Explain how a personal Google account differs from a work or school Google Workspace account
  • ✓Match each Google app to the Microsoft 365 app that does the same job
  • ✓Describe three habits of cloud apps: changes save on their own, you share a link instead of an attachment, and your files open on any computer

Lesson Notes

Read through the key concepts before you try the challenge.

Your first day at Parkview

On the job

You are Jordan Lee, the new office assistant at Parkview Property Management.

Parkview manages two apartment buildings, Elm Street Apartments and Riverside Commons. The office runs on Google Workspace: tenant letters are in Google Docs, the maintenance request log is a Google Sheet, and the staff talks over Gmail and Google Meet. Your manager, Denise Carter, set up your work account (jlee@parkviewpm.example) and wants you to know your way around before your first tenant walks in.

Your task: Know what each Google Workspace app is for, what kind of account you have, and how the Google apps compare with Microsoft Office.

Google Workspace is Google's set of apps for work and school: Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, Google Docs, Google Sheets, Google Slides, Google Meet, Google Chat, Google Forms, and more. They run in a web browser, so there is nothing to install on the computer. You sign in with one Google account and every app is there.

Google Workspace was called G Suite until October 2020. If a coworker or a job posting says G Suite, they mean the same apps.

Key terms

Google account
The sign-in you use for every Google app. It can be a personal account you create yourself or a work or school account your organization gives you.
Google Workspace
Google's apps for work and school (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Meet, Chat, Forms, and others), managed by an organization.
Cloud app
An app that runs in a web browser and keeps your files on the internet instead of on one computer.
Google Drive
Google's cloud storage. Every Doc, Sheet, and Slides file you make is saved in Drive.
Administrator (admin)
The person or IT team who manages your organization's Google Workspace accounts and settings.

The apps you will use

This course teaches Drive, Docs, and Sheets first, because almost every office task starts with a file. Later modules cover Slides, Gmail, Calendar and Meet, and working together across the apps.

Personal account or work account?

Anyone can create a free personal Google account (an address that ends in @gmail.com). A work or school account is created by an organization that pays for Google Workspace, and it usually uses the organization's own email address, like jlee@parkviewpm.example. The apps look almost the same. What changes is who is in charge of the account.

Keep work files in your work account. Do not download company files to your personal Google account or share them from it, even to work from home. If you need access from home, ask how your employer wants you to sign in.

Google Workspace and Microsoft 365

Microsoft 365 (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, OneDrive, and Teams) and Google Workspace do the same jobs. Many offices use one; plenty use both, for example Google Workspace for daily work and Word for a letter that must match a printed letterhead. If you already know a Microsoft app, most of what you know carries over.

Three habits of cloud apps

  1. Changes save on their own. Docs, Sheets, and Slides save every change to Google Drive as you type. There is no Save button. Version history keeps earlier versions in case you need to go back.
  2. You share a link, not an attachment. Instead of emailing a copy, you share the file, and everyone works in the same one at the same time. You decide who can view, comment, or edit.
  3. Your files open on any computer. Sign in on any computer with a web browser and your files are there. That is also why you must sign out on a shared computer.
Worked example

Why Denise never emails the maintenance log

Three people update the maintenance request log during the day.

  1. 1

    Keep one Google Sheet in the shared Maintenance folder in Drive.

    If each person emailed copies back and forth, nobody would know which copy is current.

  2. 2

    Share the sheet with Kim and Marcus as editors.

    Sharing gives people access to the one real file instead of making new copies.

  3. 3

    Let everyone type into it at the same time.

    Sheets saves every change for everyone, so the log is always up to date.

Result: One current log that the whole team can see and update from any computer.

🔑 In Google Workspace, keep one file and share it. Copies are for people outside the team who need a finished version.

Some Google accounts include Gemini, Google's AI assistant, which shows up as an Ask Gemini button in apps such as Docs. It needs an eligible Google Workspace or Google AI plan, and many employers turn it off or limit it. Nothing in this course requires it. If your job lets you use it, read and check everything it writes before you share it.

Challenge

Apply what you've learned in this lesson.

Look around Google Workspace in your own account. A free personal Google account works for this.

  1. Go to drive.google.com and sign in.
  2. Click the Google apps menu (the grid of dots at the top right). Write down six apps you see.
  3. Open Docs and then Sheets from the Google apps menu. Look at the home screen of each: Start a new document (or spreadsheet), the Template gallery, and your recent files.
  4. For each of these Parkview jobs, write the app you would use and one sentence why: a building notice for the lobby, a list of apartments due for smoke detector checks, a video call with the property manager at the other building.
  5. If you are on a shared computer, sign out: click your profile picture at the top right, then Sign out.
Deliverable: Submit your list of six apps and your three app choices with reasons to your instructor or course folder. If you cannot sign in to a Google account, complete the practice simulation in this lesson and submit its results page (use Print or save results on the finish card).
